newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-PUMAS FRIGHTEN BELOW-PAR ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PUMAS FRIGHTEN BELOW-PAR ENGLAND.

text.p: Argentina came within eight minutes of a famous win at Twickenham on Saturday as England scraped to a 20-18 victory which handed their critics plenty of fresh ammunition.

It took a first international try from hooker Mark Regan to rescue the home side from embarrassment on Saturday, robbing the Pumas of a first away win against the English which until then had looked distinctly possible.
They deservedly led 18-15 until England finally mounted a concerted forward challenge on their opponents' line and Regan wriggled over beneath a heap of bodies for the game's only try.

Previously fly-half Gonzalo Quesada had ruled proceedings with six sweetly-struck penalties and had he not missed his only other attempt by a whisker, the Pumas might have been beyond England's reach.
Mike Catt kept his lacklustre team in touch with five penalties of his own, but the home side's struggles were not helped by a disallowed try 15 minutes into the second-half.

Jeremy Guscott plunged over on the left but a punch from lock Martin Johnson, who was lucky to stay on the field after a swinging high tackle on Gonzalo Camardon, caused South African referee Tappe Henning to cancel the try.
Argentina led early on and were well worth a share of the halftime lead, living up to their pre-match promise to play an open brand of rugby despite freezing conditions.

They were almost responsible for one of the greatest tries seen on the ground, a magnificent passing movment from their own line carrying them deep into the English 22 where they won a penalty for a late tackle by new home captain Jason Leonard.
Queseda, a 22-year-old in only his fifth international, proved a rhythmic goalkicker in the style of the great Hugo Porta, landing three from four first-half attempts with great assurance.
His opposite number Catt had the same strike rate and the pair exchanged further penalties early in the second-half as England continued to struggle to shake off their tenacious opponents.

They even resorted to a desperate tactical substitution, bringing on Ben Clarke to beef up the back-row, but the Argentine pack gave little away and the whole Pumas side offered plenty of hope for the future.

England - 15-Nick Beal; 14-Jon Sleightholme, 13-Will Carling, 12-Jeremy Guscott, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Andy Gomarsall; 8-Chris Sheasby (19-Ben Clarke 56), 7-Lawrence Dallaglio, 6-Tim Rodber, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Martin Johnson, 3-Jason Leonard (captain), 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.

Argentina - 15-Ezequiel Jurado; 14-Gonzalo Camardon, 13- Eduardo Simone, 12-Lisandro Arbizu (captain), 11-Diego Albanese; 10-Gonzalo Queseda, 9-Nicolas Fernandez Miranda; 8-Pablo Bouza, 7-Pablo Camerlinckx, 6-Rolando Martin, 5-German Llanes, 4-Pedro Sporleder, 3-Mauricio Reggiardo, 2-Carlos Promanzio, 1-Roberto Grau.
